Question 43
?

Express z=52+4i in the form r(cos⁡θ+isin⁡θ). Give θ in radians to three decimal places.

a
52(cos⁡(5.176)+isin⁡(5.176))
b
25(cos⁡(4.381)+isin⁡(4.381))
c
25(cos⁡(1.107)+isin⁡(1.107))
d
45(cos⁡(3.871)+isin⁡(3.871))
e
52(cos⁡(0.381)+isin⁡(0.381))
Don't Know
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we express the given complex number in the form z=x+yi. To do this, we remove i from the denominator by multiplying the numerator and denominator of z by the complex conjugate of the denominator, which is 2−4i: z=52+4i=5(2−4i)(2+4i)(2−4i)=5(2−4i)22−16i2=10−20i4+16=1020−2020i=12−i.

In polar form, r represents the magnitude |z|. For a complex number z=x+yi, the magnitude of z is given by |z|=x2+y2.

So, for z=12−i, the magnitude is r=|z|=(12)2+(−1)2=14+1=54=52.

In polar form, θ represents the argument arg⁡(z). Since x=12 is positive and y=−1 is negative, z lies in the fourth quadrant. So, we can find θ as follows: θ=arg⁡(z)=2π−arctan⁡|yx|=2π−arctan⁡|(−1)(12)|=2π−arctan⁡2≈5.176, rounded to three decimal places.

Finally, we write the complex number z in polar form: z=52(cos⁡(5.176)+isin⁡(5.176)).
name: Question 43
problem: Express $z=\frac{5}{2+4\text{i}}$ in the form $r(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ).$ Give $\theta $ in radians to three decimal places.
worked_solution:
First, we express the given complex number in the form $z=x+y\text{i}.$ To do this, we remove $\text{i}$ from the denominator by multiplying the numerator and denominator of $z$ by the complex conjugate of the denominator, which is $2-4\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\frac{5}{2+4\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{5(2-4\text{i})}{(2+4\text{i})(2-4\text{i})} \\  & =\frac{5(2-4\text{i})}{{2}^{2}-16{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{10-20\text{i}}{4+16} \\  & =\frac{10}{20}-\frac{20}{20}\text{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}-\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

In polar form, $r$ represents the magnitude $|z|.$ For a complex number $z=x+y\text{i},$ the magnitude of $z$ is given by

$$
|z|=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}.
$$

So, for $z=\frac{1}{2}-\text{i},$ the magnitude is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+{(-1)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{4}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{5}{4}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In polar form, $\theta $  represents the argument $\operatorname{arg}⁡(z).$ Since $x=\frac{1}{2}$ is positive and $y=-1$ is negative, $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant. So, we can find $\theta $ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =2\pi -\operatorname{arctan}⁡|\frac{y}{x}| \\  & =2\pi -\operatorname{arctan}⁡|\frac{(-1)}{(\frac{1}{2})}| \\  & =2\pi -\operatorname{arctan}⁡2 \\  & ≈5.176,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places. 

Finally, we write the complex number $z$ in polar form:

$$
z=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(5.176)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5.176)).
$$
